newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber ends higher, March ends sharply higher.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber ends higher, March ends sharply higher.

text.p: CME lumber futures closed higher as opinions on the U.S. Commerce Department's housing report switched late in the session to slightly bullish from bearish earlier, traders said.

Also, traders said cash lumber prices continue to have a firm tone and saw mills have sold the next several weeks of production. In its midweek report, Random Lengths reported cash spruce was quoted at $403 per tbf, up $3.00 from Friday.

The U.S. Commerce Department early Wednesday reported a 12.2 percent drop in U.S. housing starts in December, which exceeded analysts' estimates. However, analysts and traders said much of the decline came in the western U.S. where flooding was severe. Elsewhere, starts were not down as much.
"The number for the year was excellent," said one trader, referring to 1.474 million units in 1996, the most since 1.488 million in 1988.
Lumber closed up $8.50 to $2.50 with March up the most at $425.80 and May up $5.70 at $391.00.
